subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Group 1
hotspots.description: This glowing column at the far left of the table is Group 1 — the alkali metals. All six members sit stacked here.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted first column of tiles below the metal cube.
hotspots.function: Shows where the alkali metals live on the periodic table.

hotspots.label: One valence electron
hotspots.description: The small atom model shows a sodium atom with just ONE electron on its outer shell — highlighted. That lonely electron is the key to the whole family.
hotspots.positionHint: The small atom model beside the cube, visible when the one-electron layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the single valence electron that drives alkali metal reactivity.

hotspots.label: Water reaction
hotspots.description: When a small piece of alkali metal meets water, it skitters and releases hydrogen and heat so fast the reaction can ignite — pure reactivity on display.
hotspots.positionHint: The small water basin below the cube's edge, visible when the reaction-test layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the violent reaction alkali metals have with water.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The alkali metal cube floats centered above a table section, lit with soft neutral studio light — the cube carries a fresh soft-silver gleam (like freshly cut metal, NOT chrome), no glow, no bloom, no emissive. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the cube is a soft silver-grey with a gentle sheen, the table tiles are paper-white with the first column faintly tinted. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / amber / molecular green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR. Cube: metallic ~0.8 (a freshly cut soft metal — nearly true metal but with a matte-ish surface), roughness ~0.3, soft silver-grey. Table tiles: paper-white, metallic 0, roughness ~0.55. Atom model: small teal electron on a translucent hairline ring. Water basin: pale translucent blue, alpha ~0.5. No emissive channels anywhere — any reaction flash is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: an alkali metal with its single outer electron and its famous water reaction, built to be read as 'the one-electron family that explodes into action.' Four procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: one smooth soft-metal cube (~0.9 cube, rounded edges) at the center, soft silver-grey with a fresh gentle sheen (metallic ~0.8, roughness ~0.3) — gleaming like a freshly cut lump of sodium. This is the star of the scene.

2) ONE ELECTRON (toggleable layer): a small atom model floats beside the cube — two translucent hairline rings (inner and outer) with tiny teal electrons filling the inner ring, and exactly ONE teal electron on the outer ring, slightly larger/brightened — the lone valence electron.

3) REACTION TEST (toggleable layer): a small shallow bowl (pale translucent blue, alpha ~0.5) appears below the cube's front edge holding 'water.' A tiny sliver of the cube drops in; the app plays a short skitter-and-fizz animation with a soft amber heat shimmer (app-driven).

4) GROUP 1 ON TABLE (toggleable layer): below, a flat section of periodic table (paper-white tiles, ~9 x 5). The entire first column is given a faint muted warm-coral cast and slight raise — Group 1.

Camera: framed so the cube is large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: AlkaliCube, ShellAtom, InnerElectrons, ValenceElectron, WaterBasin, ReactionSliver, TableSlab, Group1Column. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
